title: The New Red Sea Wars
gist: Teaser of an International Crisis Group analyst's argument that Sudan's three-year civil war has become a regional proxy war, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio publicly blaming Saudi Arabia and the UAE for frustrating peace efforts. The piece frames conflicts in the Middle East and the Horn of Africa as now inseparable around the Red Sea.

insights.claim: On June 3, 2026, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told Congress that Sudan's three-year war had become a proxy war and blamed Saudi Arabia and the UAE for frustrating US efforts to end it.
insights.so_what: Open US criticism of two key Gulf partners signals friction in Washington-Gulf relations.
insights.quote: Rubio told the U.S. Congress that the fighting that had raged for three years in Sudan was now a “proxy war”
insights.locator: On June 3, U.S. Secretary of State
insights.speaker: Alan Boswell

insights.claim: Alan Boswell argues Sudan's conflict has morphed from a domestic power struggle into a wider regional war drawing in outside powers and spilling across its borders.
insights.so_what: A widening Sudan war raises instability risk along a vital shipping corridor.
insights.quote: what started as a domestic power struggle has morphed into a wider regional war, drawing in outside powers and spilling across Sudan’s borders.
insights.speaker: Alan Boswell

insights.claim: Boswell contends that conflicts in the Middle East and the Horn of Africa have become inseparable, with Sudan's spreading war part of a larger geopolitical transformation around the Red Sea.
insights.so_what: Red Sea and Bab el Mandeb shipping risk should be assessed as a single linked theater rather than isolated conflicts.
insights.quote: The spread of the conflict in Sudan is part of a larger geopolitical transformation.
insights.locator: The spread of the conflict in Sudan
insights.speaker: Alan Boswell
